The epitope residues for the mAb were determined by analysis of binding activity to wild-type (WT) and mutant RBD measured by ELISA. The mutagenesis study substituted ACE2-interactive and noninteractive residues with alanine or arginine in RBD. Mutant residues reducing binding activity by more than 75% compared to binding to wild type RBD are identified as critical residues. Mutation N343A, T345A, K417A, G447R, Y453A F456A, E465A, R466A, V483A, N487A, Q493A or T500R reduced binding of mAb P02-3C11. Glycan modiﬁcation at positions D420 and A475 or K458 and A475 destroyed the binding of mAb P02-3C11.

interactions.assay: in vivo assay · pathogen burden after challenge after adoptive transfer
interactions.note: Prophylactic or therapeutic administration of the epitope specific mAb alone or in combination with the RBD specific mAb, COV--2381, protected animals from SARS-CoV 2 infection and was dependent on Fc function.  mAb therapy reduced weight loss, viral burden, lung pathology, and multiple cytokine/chemokine levels.
The residues for the epitope specific mAb were determined by alanine scanning mutagenesis with an additional residue determined by viral escape mutants.

The epitope specific mAb bound to cells infected with the wildtype SARS-CoV2 n-CoV/USA/WA1/2020 strain, but did not bind to cells infected with the WA1 strain pseudotyped with the S protein from the B1.351 variant.  Binding to the B.1.1.7 variant was minimally affected.
Binding of the epitope specific mAb to the stabilized trimeric form of the S protein in the closed configuration was visualized by negative stain electron microscopy.

The epitope specific mAb bound to the stabilized trimeric form of the S protein, but failed to bind to soluble recombinant NTD protein.  Mutation of the Fc portion of the mAb which abrogated interaction of the Fc with Fcgamma receptors and complement did not affect binding of the mAb to the antigen.  Binding by the mAb to the epitope is competed by binding of the NTD specific mAb, COV-2489, and some convalescent patient sera.
